findings.title: Implemented A6-P2 fold boundaries are the A9 SENSITIVITY freeze, not the A9 primary frozen fold contract
findings.detail: family_a6p2.FOLD_BOUNDARIES_P2 = (2020-09-09, 2023-02-16) are the calendar thirds of the full S0 window - the block that d2/a9_feasibility/FXFV6-A6-P2.json itself labels sensitivity_fold_thirds_full_S0_grid. The A9 verdict (d2_a9_feasibility_verdict.json measurement_basis.fold_freeze) FROZE the A6 folds 'on the funded 7-pair common decision-day grid: F1 2018-09-03..2020-12-18, F2 2020-12-21..2023-04-05, F3 2023-04-06..2025-07-24' - which is also the proposal's dominant literal reading ('3 contiguous temporal thirds of S0 by decision-day count'; calendar-even thirds including the 152-day pre-data head are not thirds by decision-day count). The I1 reading justifying the adoption ('the only in-repo frozen-boundary evidence is the sensitivity block') is factually contradicted by the A9 verdict's own fold_freeze field. Measured impact at HEAD: implemented fold populations (dry-run temp ledger) are 104/346/247 (anchor) vs the A9 frozen/measured 143/322/230. Eligibility floors clear under both partitions, but the SCORED family-killing gates ('anchor identifying metric <= 0 in ANY of the 3 held-out fold evaluations -> REJECT'; 'pooled per-trade net mean > 0 at stress tier 2.0 in EACH held-out fold') would be adjudicated on a partition that differs from the frozen and D2-measured one. The scored ledger is append-only and the no-rescue rule forbids changing folds after PnL is visible, so launching now would irreversibly bind the cycle to non-frozen boundaries.
